Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 28-Dec-2024 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.Tech. (COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING) / FIFTH SEMESTER INTEGRATED MSC -  
  MATHEMATICS AND COMPUTING DEGREE EXAMINATION - DECEMBER 2024 / JANUARY 2025  
  SUBJECT: CSE 2124/CSE_2124 - OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING  
  OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING [CSE 2124]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  a  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Develop a Java program to operate employee payroll system for the industry. The program             (3)  
  should be developed to support the following operations. (i) Add any new employee to the system  
  (unique integer for each employee id ) and name (String for employee's name), (ii) Calculate weekly  
  pay for the employee based on the hours worked for a given week, (iii) Search for employees who  
  worked overtime (more than 40 hours).Use an array of Employee objects to store the list of  
  employees. Implement a menu-driven interface using control structures to navigate each  
  operation. The weekly pay is calculated as follows:For a total of 40 hours or less: weeklyPay =  
  totalHours * hourlyWage. For more than 40 hours: weeklyPay = (40 * hourlyWage) +  
  (overtimeHours * 1.5 * hourlyWage).  
1B)               Design and develop the Java code for the given scenario. Consider an online store which sells        (4)  
  grocery products such as rice, wheat, milk, sugar. Create a class called Store which has instance  
  variable like Product name, Product ID, Product category, Product price. Create four instance  
  of the class and call two methods. setdetails: set details of the product one and displaydetails:for  
  displaying the details of the product. Further write a method named compare and call it wherein it  
  takes the object of the class as argument and compares the prices of the product and display  
  appropriate message.(message like "product1" cheaper than "product2")  
1C)               Show a complete Java program to do the following:                                                    (3)  
  i) Accept two strings S1 and S2. Find the common Substrings from the two input strings.  
  Example:  
  S1: Python is new and vibrant  
  S2: Work is full of new experiences.  
  Then two common substrings found are "is" and "new".  
  Replace the string "is" with "are" in S1 and S2 . ThenDisplay the modified strings.  
2A)               Develop an abstract base class named Vehicle that includes attributes such as vehicleType            (5)  
  (String e.g., "Car", "Truck", "Motorcycle"), fuelLevel (an integer and as a percentage from 0  
  to 100), isEngineRunning (a boolean indicating if the engine is running), and mileage (a  
  double representing the number of kilometers driven). The Vehicle class should have the  
  following methods:  
  startEngine(): starting the engine and reduces the fuel level by 1% for every engine start.  
  stopEngine() : which sets isEngineRunning to false and increases the fuel level by 0.5% when the  
  engine is stopped.  
  checkFuelLevel() :which prints the current fuel level and advises refueling if below 10%  
  accelerate() : acceleration, increases mileage by 10 km, and reduces fuel by 2% for every 10 km  
  driven.  
  Next, create a derived class named Car that extends the Vehicle class and overrides the  
  startEngine() method to reduce fuel by 2% instead of 1% on engine start, and theaccelerate()  
  method to simulate fuel consumption, decreasing the fuel level by 2% for every 10 kilometers  
  driven. The Car class should also implement the Electric interface, which includes a method  
  Page 1 of 3

chargeBattery() to simulate charging the battery. This method should increase the battery level by  
  10% per cycle, ensuring it does not exceed 100%.  
  In Main class with a main method, anobject of the Car class need to create, and demonstrate the  
  functionality of the Vehicle and Electric methods by simulating engine starts, fuel consumption and  
  battery charging. Include logic to print the vehicle's current fuel level, mileage, and battery status  
  after each action.  
2B)   Build a Java program to create a Generic class Shape, that can handle different data types for the (3)  
  length and width of a shape (for example, Integer, Double, etc.). The class should be designed to  
  compute the Area based on the length and width provided and should support the following  
  requirements: Use bounded types to ensure that only numeric types (such as Integer, Double,  
  etc.) can be passed as the Generic parameter T. Define two attributes, length and width, both of  
  type T. Define a method calculateArea() that returns the area as a double. Write a static method  
  displayArea that accepts a Shape object with any numeric type (Integer, Double, etc.) and  
  displays the area. In the Main class, create different instances of the Shape class with different  
  numeric types for length and width (e.g., Integer, Double). Use the displayArea method to calculate  
  and display the area of each shape.  
2C)   In a library management application, you have two packages: books and members. The Book   (2)  
  class in books needs access to the Member class in members. However, the Member class has  
  package-private methods. Why can't Book access the package-private methods of Member?  
  What access modifier would allow Book to access those methods?  
3A)   Create a class Order with data members ID and cuisine that represents the order number and                (3)  
  cuisine of a dish ordered by a customer at a restaurant. The different cuisines that the restaurant  
  serves are stored in a string array, cuisines which is a variable within ICuisine interface. Create a  
  class OrderDemo with main() that initializes an array of Order objects. All the orders must be  
  checked if they can be served or not through checkCuisine(Order[] o) of Order. An order cannot be  
  served if its specified cuisine is not in cuisines array. Handle this scenario by throwing  
  CuisineUnavailableException that displays a suitable message such as "Cuisnie: Lebanese of  
  Order:102 cannot be served."  
3B)   Build a Java program that uses the Runnable interface with the following functionality: The matrix of (5)  
  size M X M is taken from the user in main (). Create one child thread to calculate the primary  
  diagonal sum and another child thread to calculate the last column sum. If the sums are equal, the  
  main thread should display the message "Entered matrix is a magic matrix".  
3C)   Write a Java program that demonstrates thread communication between two threads using wait()              (2)  
  and notify() to display "Ping" and "Pong" alternately.  
4A)   Define a generic Numberclass with 1D array reference as an instance variable, a parameterized             (4)  
  constructor that takes only one parameter, Sort() to sort the array in ascending order using bubble  
  sort method, disp() to display the array elements using for-each loop. Write a driver class to test all  
  methods of Numberclass for Integer and Double types.  
4B)   Create a class BookAvailability with bookCount as a data member that keeps track of total number (4)  
  of books available. Provide two methods reserve(int n) and cancel(int m) that are invoked whenever  
  a book has to be reserved or cancelled concurrently. These methods also display the ticketCount  
  after their respective tasks. Create at least two threads to reserve a book and one to cancel using  
  BookTransaction class that implements Runnable interface. Demonstrate the instantiation, creation  
  of the above threads along with implementation of the reserve and cancel methods suitably.  
4C)   Demonstrate with an example how the CERT rule to validate return values of a method is                    (2)  
  beneficial.  
5A)   Write a JavaFX program that creates a simple calculator with the following features:                      (4)  
  
  Use two TextField elements for the user to input two numbers.  
  Provide a ComboBox for selecting one of the following operations: Add, Subtract, Multiply,  
  and Divide.  
  Add a Button labelled Calculate that performs the selected operation when clicked.  
  Display the result or any validation message (e.g., if the fields are left empty or the user  
  attempts to divide by zero) in a Label below the button.  
  
  
5B)   Write a JavaFX application such that a user creates two text fields and enters radius and color,          (4)  
  Page 2 of 3

where color can take values of red, green and blue. Create a push button with name Render on it.  
The application should render a circle of the entered radius and color using Canvas. Use FlowPane  
layout.
